follow-up time: Through delivery and postpartum period (breastfeeding duration mentioned)
exposure: Black and Hispanic women were compared separately to White women.
cohort: 294 women with multiple sclerosis (81 Black, 67 Hispanic, and 146 White) who delivered live births between 2010 and 2021
finding: Underrepresented women (Black and Hispanic) with MS entered pregnancy with higher disability and fewer healthcare resources compared to White women, and their babies had lower birthweights and shorter breastfeeding duration.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery differed significantly between racial/ethnic groups; Black women had the highest rates of emergency cesarean deliveries, and Hispanic women had the highest rates of uncomplicated vaginal deliveries.
birth_weight: Median birth weight: 3,198 g for babies born to underrepresented women vs. 3,275 g for babies born to White women
